posts.style: Design & Aspiration · The Kitchen That Sits Under the Beam
posts.alt: A Rancho Santa Fe Spanish Colonial backyard at golden hour: sand stucco with a clay barrel-tile roof, a bronze pergola over a long dining table beside an outdoor kitchen with a stone veneer island, built-in grill and a wood-fired pizza oven, an ivory porcelain patio, a round copper fire bowl with curved stone seating, olive trees, agave and lavender, with neighboring Spanish-style homes visible close by on both sides and beyond the wall
posts.hook: The best outdoor kitchens are the ones where the cook never leaves the conversation.
posts.caption:
Most outdoor kitchens end up in a corner, a long walk from the table. Whoever is cooking spends the evening alone with the grill.

This one is built the other way around. The island sits directly under the same beam as the dining table, so the cook, the oven and the dinner guests share one room. The pizza oven faces the patio. The fire bowl is ten steps away, with a curved stone seat for the part of the night after the plates are cleared. Olive trees and lavender keep the whole thing softly Spanish, and quiet enough to hear the fire.

The selections:
• Trex Pergola in bronze over the dining and kitchen
• Eldorado Stone veneer island with Lynx built-in grill
• wood-fired pizza oven in a matching stone surround
• Belgard Porcelain patio in ivory
• Bobe fire bowl with curved stone seat wall
• olive, lavender & agave · FX Luminaire path lighting

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Curved Drive
posts.alt: The front of a two-story Spanish-style home in Rolling Hills Ranch, Chula Vista, at golden hour: warm sand stucco with a terracotta tile roof and arched entry, a wide curving driveway of grey-tan Belgard Mega-Arbel pavers with a charcoal border, a matching walk and steps, stone-veneer raised planters with agave, an olive tree, sago palms and kangaroo paw in decomposed granite, bronze path lights, with neighboring tile-roof homes visible close by down the street
posts.hook: A driveway that curves toward the door reads as an invitation. One that runs straight at the garage reads as a parking lot.
posts.caption:
Master-planned neighborhoods like Rolling Hills Ranch give every home a good facade. What separates one from the next is the ground in front of it.

Here the drive bends gently toward the entry instead of running flat at the garage, with a dark soldier-course border drawing the curve in one clean line. The walk and steps pick up the same paver so the whole approach reads as one piece. Stone-veneer planters hold the corner, and the planting stays low and sculptural: agave, sago, kangaroo paw and a single olive over a bed of decomposed granite. It looks composed in every season and asks very little of anyone.

The front yard is the first room of the house. Build it like one.

The selections:
• Belgard Mega-Arbel pavers in a grey-tan blend with a charcoal border
• Eldorado Stone veneer raised planters
• olive tree, agave, sago palms & kangaroo paw in decomposed granite
• Kichler bronze path lights & uplighting

Want a front approach with some intention behind it? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Craft & Process · The Slope Becomes the Seating
posts.alt: A Mount Helix hillside backyard at golden hour behind a mid-century modern ranch home of board-formed concrete and cedar: terraced Techo-Bloc stacked retaining walls, wide stepped stairs, a sunken lounge with a linear fire feature and built-in stone seating, agave, barrel cactus, aloe and ornamental grasses, with mountains and neighboring homes visible close by across the slope
posts.hook: On a hillside, the retaining wall is not the problem to hide. It's the architecture to show.
posts.caption:
Mount Helix yards come with grade, and the usual response is to hide it: bury it behind one tall wall and flatten whatever is left. The better move is to use it.

Here the slope is stepped into terraces, and each wall does two jobs. The upper walls hold the hill and frame the stairs. The lower ones wrap a sunken lounge, so the same stone that retains the earth also seats the family around a linear flame. From the house the whole thing reads as a single piece of sculpture, with the mountains behind it.

What you don't see is the part that matters most: engineered footings, compacted base, drainage behind every wall. That's the work we spend the most time on.

The selections:
• Techo-Bloc Industria stacked retaining & seat walls
• Warming Trends linear fire feature
• wide stepped stone stairs & travertine-tone coping
• agave, barrel cactus, aloe & ornamental grasses
• FX Luminaire wall-wash lighting

posts.style: Drone Aerial · One Lot, Three Rooms
posts.alt: A drone aerial at golden hour of a Millenia, Chula Vista family backyard between neighboring tile-roof homes: a green and blue pickleball court beside a SYNLawn turf lawn, a paver patio with a bronze pergola and lounge seating, a round stone fire pit with curved seating, raised planters with olive trees and agave, and wood fences with neighboring backyards close by on all sides
posts.hook: From above you can see the plan: a court, a lounge and a fire pit on one normal lot.
posts.caption:
On a standard suburban lot, the question is rarely whether there's enough room. It's whether the room is organized.

From the air it's easy to read. A pickleball court takes the far end, with turf on either side so the rest of the yard stays soft. A pergola and lounge anchor the house side, one step from the kitchen door. A round fire pit with a curved seat wall sits in the corner, where the evening ends up. Raised planters and olive trees keep the fence lines from feeling like fence lines.

Three rooms, one lot, nothing fighting for the same square foot.

The selections:
• SnapSports pickleball court in green and blue
• SYNLawn turf lawn & borders
• Belgard Urbana paver patio
• Trex Pergola in bronze
• stone-veneer fire pit with curved seat wall
• olive & agave in raised planters

posts.style: Seasonal · The Longest Night · Winter Solstice Eve
posts.alt: A La Jolla hillside backyard at blue-hour dusk before the winter solstice: a black louvered pergola with a simple olive-branch garland and warm string lights over a teak dining table with white linen, candle lanterns and artichokes, a lit copper fire bowl with built-in cushioned seating, silver travertine terrace, stacked-stone walls, citrus, palms and agave, a sliver of ocean on the horizon, and neighboring coastal homes with glowing windows close by on the hillside
posts.hook: The longest night of the year is a good excuse to set a table outside.
posts.caption:
The winter solstice is Monday, and in San Diego it doesn't mean the yard goes dark. It means the evening starts early, the air cools, and the fire finally earns its place.

This terrace is built for exactly that night. A louvered roof overhead keeps the table dry and the light low. A simple olive garland and a few candles are all it takes to make it feel like the season. A fire bowl sits in the middle of built-in seating, so the conversation drifts there after dinner, and the whole hillside glows below.

No ornaments needed. The yard does the work.

The selections:
• StruXure louvered pergola in black
• Bobe fire bowl in copper with built-in cushioned seating
• silver travertine terrace by Bedrosians
• Eldorado Stone walls
• citrus, palms & agave · FX Luminaire & string lighting
